description: Source-independent DTC severity rule table (SAE J2012 subsystem x fault-type). Derives `severity` for every DTC instead of trusting scraped source text. See docs: AGENTS.md 2.3 (no fabricated telemetry / no invented severity) and the 2026-09-21 deep-discovery finding P0-1.
_authority: SAE J2012 diagnostic trouble code semantics. A code's severity is a function of WHICH subsystem fails and HOW it fails, not of whether a scraped page used the word 'critical'.
_unknown_policy: No rule matches -> UNKNOWN (never INVENT a rung, never default to MEDIUM). `Severity.UNKNOWN` maps to GRAY in drive_safety_policy.decide_risk (never GREEN), so an unclassifiable fault fails safe.

critical_stop_allowlist._comment: The ONLY code families that may be CRITICAL_STOP: faults that can destroy the engine/transmission or remove a primary safety function while driving. Everything else is capped at HIGH. This is a CLOSED list - the regression test fails if an unlisted code carries CRITICAL_STOP.

family_rules.note: Communication loss WITH the engine/transmission controller itself removes engine control -> stop-worthy only for the specific allowlisted U0100/U0101/U0102.
Any other module communication loss degrades a function (ABS/park-brake/trailer/CAN electrical) but does not require stopping the engine -- YELLOW, not RED.

subsystem_caps._comment: Hard ceiling per SAE J2012 code class. A body/comfort code can NEVER be CRITICAL_STOP regardless of what a source page claimed.

fault_type_penalties._comment: Within a subsystem, the failure MODE scales severity. Applied AFTER subsystem cap. `heater`, `circuit_open`, `lamp`, `comfort` faults are never stop-the-engine.

fault_type_patterns._comment: Keyword -> fault type. Matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY against the DTC title. Order matters: first match wins, so the most severe pattern must be listed first.

misfire_rule._comment: Discovery finding P0-1: P0301-P0312 (single-cylinder misfire) were CRITICAL_STOP while P0300 (random/multiple misfire) was MEDIUM - inverted. A single-cylinder misfire is LESS severe than a random/multiple misfire. Both are MEDIUM (drive-on, service soon); a misfire only escalates to CRITICAL_STOP when a catalyst-damage code (P0420/P0430) or misfire-with-fuel-cutoff condition is simultaneously present, which this table does not infer.

structural_fault_modes._comment: SAE J2012 titles follow a rigid grammar. After the explicit fault_type_patterns, these structural rules classify the remaining titles by their standard suffix. This is NOT keyword-scraping: every pattern is SAE's own title vocabulary, and the rung reflects the documented failure mode (an electrical circuit fault degrades a function; it does not stop the engine).

provenance.derived_from: SAE J2012 / SAE J1979 DTC semantics
provenance._apology: This table encodes SAE subsystem semantics only. It contains NO vehicle-specific thresholds and NO fabricated field values; every rung is a documented SAE classification (AGENTS.md 2.3).
